🐣 Start from zero · Step 5 of 5 · 5 min

Train your first model

Find the number that makes the fewest mistakes.

📏 A tiny model: one rule, one number

A model can be tiny: just one rule with one number in it. The rule below is a model like that. It sorts messages into spam and not spam, and the letter T stands for its number.

In machine learning, nobody writes T by hand: it has to be found from examples. A number that a model learns from examples is called a parameter.

IF a message has more than T exclamation marks, THEN it is spam.
Otherwise it is not spam.

Spam means messages that nobody asked for, like adverts sent to thousands of people.

📋 Six examples with the right answers

To find T, the model needs examples. The table below shows six messages: the number of exclamation marks in each one, and whether it really is spam. A person has checked every message and written down the right answer.

The examples that a model learns from are called its training data.

Exclamation marksIt really is
0not spam
1not spam
3not spam
4spam
6spam
9spam

Task. Start with a guess: T = 0. Now the model says “spam” when a message has more than 0 exclamation marks, and “not spam” otherwise. On how many of the six examples is it wrong?

Show the solution

On 2. The messages with 1 and 3 exclamation marks are not spam, but the model calls them spam. Its other four answers are right. That includes the message with 0 marks: 0 is not more than 0, so the model says “not spam”.

Task. Try another number: T = 5. Now the model says “spam” only when a message has more than 5 exclamation marks. How many mistakes does it make on the six examples?

Show the solution

Just 1. The message with 4 exclamation marks is spam, but 4 is not more than 5, so the model lets it through. That is better than with T = 0, but still not perfect.

Task. A model says “spam” when a message has more than T exclamation marks, and “not spam” otherwise. The table shows six messages with the right answers. For which whole number T is the model right about all six?

Show the solution

T = 3. Then the messages with 4, 6 and 9 marks are called spam, and the ones with 0, 1 and 3 are not: no mistakes. With T = 2 the message with 3 marks would be called spam too, and with T = 4 the spam message with 4 marks would get through. T is the model's parameter: a number found from examples.

🔁 That was training

You did it: your first model is trained! That is what training is: try a number, count the mistakes, try another, and keep the one with the fewest mistakes.

A computer does the same, only with far more numbers. A big model can have millions or even billions of parameters and learn from millions of examples.

And the computer does not guess blindly. It looks at the mistakes, moves every parameter a little so that the mistakes get smaller, and repeats this again and again. Most of today's AI models learn like this.

Task. What does it mean to “train” an AI model?

Show the answer

Right answer: To find the parameters: the numbers that give the fewest mistakes on its examples

Training is a search for the model's parameters: the numbers with which it makes the fewest mistakes on its examples. Nobody writes them by hand. And the model does not need to keep the examples: what it keeps is the numbers it has found.

🆕 The real test: a new message

Your model with T = 3 makes no mistakes on its six examples. But a model is made for new messages, the ones it has never seen. Here comes one.

A friend writes: “Happy birthday!!!!!” That is 5 exclamation marks, and 5 is more than 3. So the model says: spam.

Wrong: it is a greeting from a friend! The model was perfect on its six examples, and it still fails on a new one.

Task. Why did the model call the birthday message spam?

Show the answer

Right answer: Its six examples had no friendly message with more than 3 exclamation marks

A model knows only what was in its examples. In them, every message with more than 3 exclamation marks was spam, so the model learned “more than 3 marks means spam”. It counted correctly, and T = 3 fits the six examples best. The trouble was the examples: too few and too one-sided.

Think first. How would you make this model better?

Show the answer

Give it more examples, and more kinds of them: friendly messages with many exclamation marks too.

Let it look at more than one clue: with exclamation marks alone, it cannot tell a happy friend from an advert. The words (“free”, “win”), the sender and the links help too. Real spam filters can use thousands of clues, each with its own parameter.

And always test it on examples it has never seen. In the AI Lab, the experiment “Build a spam filter” lets you teach a filter that looks at the words, and test it on new messages.

Task. A model makes no mistakes on the examples it was trained on. What does that say about new examples?

Show the answer

Right answer: Not much: it has to be tested on examples it has never seen

The model has already seen its training examples, so getting them right proves little. On new ones it may do well or badly: only a test on examples it has never seen can show which.

Remember

  • A model is a rule with numbers in it. The numbers are called parameters: they are not written by hand but found from examples.
  • Training is a search for the parameters: try them on the training data, count the mistakes and keep the ones that give fewer mistakes.
  • A model is only as good as its examples.
  • The real test is on examples the model has never seen.
